scoreRationale: The sparse locality has no independent visitor-centre depth; House of Dun is correctly separated as a 94-point attraction.

namedTrailSearch.TreasureTrails: No exact Dun or House of Dun product in the current Dundee and Angus collection.
retained: Lady Augusta's Walk and Den of Dun
House of Dun to Montrose Basin Hide

practicalAudit.eat: Erskine's Cafe is the sole qualifying coffee, baking and light-lunch stop; menu, prices, seasonal hours and dog access are published.
practicalAudit.picnic: Official picnic areas are confirmed in the courtyard and grounds; table count is not published.
practicalAudit.parking: Official £5 pay-and-display visitor parking, free to NTS members; capacity is not published and accessible bays are separately documented.
practicalAudit.toilets: Courtyard toilets include accessible provision and baby changing during visitor-facility hours.
practicalAudit.accessibility: Step-free access reaches the courtyard, cafe, shop and part of the house; upper rooms remain stair-only. Estate path surfaces vary.
practicalAudit.transport: Bus stops on the A935 around half a mile from the house; Montrose station is four miles away.

exclusions: House of Dun does not raise the settlement score.
Period-unassigned NRHE survey records remain stored but hidden.
